title: Wickaposset (Fishers Island)
summary: A small eastern-island place name whose variants preserve older coastal geography beyond the main body of Long Island.
introduction_content: Wickaposset is a Fisher's Island place-name, with Wecopesuck and Wicapeset as recorded variants. The name is associated with the eastern end of the island in Southold town.
history_content: The name is connected with a point of land and with J. Hammond Trumbull's description of a small rocky island at the east end of Fishers Island. The exact historic point or rock requires site-level review.
translation_content:
The interpretation is "little thing at the end," analyzed through Algonquian terms meaning "at the end" and "a small thing." Wickaposset is also listed as a see-reference to Wickapogue, but the Fisher's Island location is distinct from the Southampton Meacox Bay placename.

Why Place Names Matter

“Many Native American place names have suffered mutilation at the hands of their writers, making accurate translation into the English language very difficult today.”

— Nipmuc Indian Association of Connecticut, The Nipmuc People, Their Territory & Language (1994), Territory and Language page, paragraph on spelling

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: Wickaposset preserves a localized Fishers Island placename, but the source does not establish which exact point or small rocky island was intended.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement at the east end of Fishers Island, based on a source description of a point or small rocky island there. Coordinates are not exact historic coordinates and are offset slightly for map visibility.
